newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa sells 9.7 pct stake in Scor.
newsitem.headline: Axa sells 9.7 pct stake in Scor.

text.p: French insurer Axa said it had sold its 9.7 percent stake in the country's leading reinsurer Scor, making a 22.5 million franc net capital gain.
Axa, which is developing its own reinsurance activities through Abeille Re which it bought last year, had already indicated that it wanted to dispose of its stake.

Traders had reported a sharp rise in the volume of Scor shares traded in the past few days. An Axa spokeswoman had said the disposal was carried out throughout July and August with the last transaction on August 28.
An Axa spokeswoman cited good market conditions for the sale's timing.
"We didn't consider it to be a strategic holding and we said if the right opportunity came along to dispose of it, we would do so," she said.
The value of shares in Scor, which announced in June it would list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange by year end, have climbed by 33.3 percent since the start of the year.
The shares were reported to be listed in Axa's books as having an average value of 150 francs. Scor shares on Thursday finished down 1.9 percent at 204 francs.
Scor's largest shareholder, Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP), has said it might cut its 40 percent stake in Scor when it lists in New York as Scor was not a core holding.

There has been a wave of consolidation sweeping the global reinsurance sector and Scor's shares have been helped recently by speculation that it might become a target for takeover by a large U.S. reinsurer.
